HackLab #2 Berlin · Prior Labs track “TabPFN for spatial awareness” · 21–22 Nov 2026

Can a table steady a crane load?

We turned an overhead crane’s motion into a table, one row every 0.1 s, and asked TabPFN, a model that learns from the examples it is shown rather than from training, to predict where the swinging load will be 1 s later and to choose the anti-sway setting for each new load.

The whole project in four sentences

A crane’s load keeps swinging after every move, and anti-sway only cancels it if someone types in the right sling length. We log the crane’s own motion as table rows and give them to TabPFN as examples. It predicts where the load will be 1 s later, 5–7× closer than physics with a wrong length, and before each move it picks the anti-sway setting with the shortest safe wait. It learns a new load in a few cycles without retraining, but timing the set-down alone does not work: the swing has to be killed.

01

Prior Labs and TabPFN

In simple words

Most AI models must be trained on your data before they can predict anything. TabPFN was trained once by Prior Labs, on millions of made-up tables, to do one thing well: read a table of examples and fill in the answer for a new row, with a range. For a crane, a new load needs no retraining: its rows are simply added to the table.

How TabPFN differs from a normal model

The model we use

ItemValue
VersionTabPFN-3.5 (open weights, tabpfn 10.2), run locally
Pre-trainingmillions of synthetic tables (Hollmann et al., Nature 2025)
Our context3,000 rows for the forecast; 120–150 moves for the anti-sway choice
Outputa distribution: quantiles 5 / 50 / 95% (forecast), 50 / 99% (choice)
Speed trickfit_with_cache: the context is encoded once
Speedabout 2 ms per row predicted; a refit takes about 7 s (GTX 1650 laptop)
Licenceopen weights, non-commercial

02

The crane, real and simulated

In simple words

An overhead crane carries a hanging load along a rail. Every time it speeds up or stops, the load swings, and it can’t be set down until the swing dies. Anti-sway control cancels the swing with two half-sized pushes, but only if it knows the swing period, which comes from a sling length the operator types in. Typed in wrong, the swing survives and the crane waits.

Real lab cranepublic data
Tower crane at Nazarbayev University: cables 0.1–0.8 m, three payload shapes, hoisting. 33 runs of 99 s at 100 Hz (Alhassan et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0).
Full-size craneMuJoCo
Trolley, 3–6 m rope, hook, 0.5–3 m slings, 0.4–3 t beam, racks beside two bays. Its swing period matches the double-pendulum formula (5.11 s vs 5.06 s).
Industry anti-swayZV shaper
Splits every speed change into two half pushes, half a swing period apart (Singer & Seering 1990). The period comes from the typed-in sling length.
03

Our implementation

In simple words

Step 1: log the crane’s motion as rows, one every 0.1 s. Step 2: give TabPFN the rows it has as examples. Step 3: every 0.1 s ask where the load will be in 1 s; before each move, ask how much swing each anti-sway setting will leave. Step 4: one second later the true answer is known, and that row joins the table. Nothing is trained.

Two questions we ask TabPFN

QuestionInputsAnswerTable it reads
Where will the load be in 1 s?12: swing now, 0.2 s and 0.5 s ago, swing rate, recent swing size; trolley position, speed, acceleration; rope length, payload; planned move in 0.5 s and 1 sload offset 1 s ahead, with a 90% range3,000 rows of past jobs + this load’s own rows
How much swing will this setting leave?3: measured swing period, speed, tuning error (assumed vs measured period)swing left (median and 99%) and settle time120–150 commissioning moves + this load’s moves (weighted 5×)

A setting already tried on the current load uses its measured result instead of the prediction.

04

Results

In simple words

As a forecaster, TabPFN beats physics whenever physics is given the wrong length, and it adapts to a new load from a few seconds of its rows. Used to choose the anti-sway, it cut the time for 12 new loads by 35%. Where physics knows the true length, physics is as good or better.

4e · Could we just time the set-down? (experiment F)

When to start lowering (12 industry anti-sway moves)Inside ±5 cm at touchdownSideways speed at touchdownSafe touchdown
Physics predicts inside ±5 cm4 / 1213 cm/s0 / 12
TabPFN: whole 90% range inside ±5 cm12 / 1215 cm/s0 / 12
What it says

TabPFN knows where the load will be, but a swinging load passes through the target at about 15 cm/s, so no timing makes the touchdown safe. The gain has to come from killing the swing (4c). Where timing does win: magnet and grab cranes that release mid-swing.

4f · Which inputs matter? (experiment G)

Forecast inputsError 1 s ahead, new jobsError, 81-setting sweep
All 120.78 cm0.95 cm
6: swing, rate, 0.5 s history, rope, push0.92 cm1.49 cm
4: swing, rate, push (no rope length)1.87 cm2.00 cm

The forecast needs all 12 inputs. The anti-sway choice is as good with 3 (period, speed, tuning error: 2.57 s settle error) as with 5 (2.51 s).

05

Limitations

In simple words

The real data is a small lab crane, the full-size results are simulation, and TabPFN only helps where physics has a wrong number: with the true length, physics is as good.

Lab-scale real data< 1 m
Cables under 1 m, payloads under 1 kg, one run per condition.
Simulation for full size1 seed
Industrial-size results are MuJoCo, one seed each.
Physics wins on known lengths0.34 vs 1.52 cm
On a new real cable length the corrected pendulum beats TabPFN.
Early mistakes2 of 9
Live, it misses a cycle or two before its own rows of the new load build up.
Timing alone fails15 cm/s
The swing has to be killed; predicting it is not enough.
No safety proof0 collisions
No strategy collided, so the gains shown are time, not accidents avoided.
Slow refits on a laptop≈7 s
The live forecast video was rendered offline.
Licencenon-commercial
A product needs a Prior Labs licence.
Hackathon time~29 h
The ideas below were not yet run.

07

Glossary

TabPFN
Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network: a transformer pre-trained on synthetic tables that predicts the answer for new rows from example rows, with no training.
Context
The example rows TabPFN reads. Here: past crane rows plus the current load’s own rows.
Swing (load offset)
How far the load hangs to the side of the trolley, in metres.
Swing period
Time for one full swing back and forth; longer rope and sling, slower swing.
Sling
The straps between hook and load. Its length changes with every load and is typed in by the operator.
Anti-sway (ZV shaper)
Splits each speed change into two half pushes half a swing period apart, so the swings they start cancel.
Setting (tuning)
The sling length the anti-sway assumes. This is what TabPFN chooses; TabPFN itself is never tuned.
Settle time
Wait after a move until the load stays inside ±5 cm and can be set down.
90% range
TabPFN’s interval that should contain the true value 90% of the time.
Closed loop
The crane acts on TabPFN’s answers, and the result becomes the next row.
MuJoCo
A physics engine for robots; it simulates the crane, rope and load.
